$comment: Hand-maintained input of build_third_party.py. Everything here is either (a) a pointer to a plain file in TEMP/, (b) provenance that was checked on the date in 'accessed' (URLs listed were actually opened), or (c) SEM Lab's own proposals. Nothing here was extracted from the encrypted SmartPLS project files.
proposalLabel: SEM Lab specification — not extracted from the SmartPLS project file

statusVocabulary.redistributable-with-attribution: A licence was found at the source and it permits redistribution with attribution.
statusVocabulary.terms-unverified: No licence or terms covering redistribution were found at the sources opened. Do not publish in a public build until the owner clears it.
statusVocabulary.restricted: Terms were found and they forbid redistribution.

provenance.origin: Survey of 1,190 computer users in Saudi Arabia. The SmartPLS sample-project page attributes the data to Anderson, Al-Gahtani & Hubona (2011) and says Al-Gahtani, Hubona & Wang (2007), Al-Gahtani & Shih (2009) and Anderson et al. (2011) describe the data and the model.
provenance.licence: None stated. The SmartPLS sample-project page and the SmartPLS terms and conditions say nothing about reuse or redistribution of sample data. No public deposit of the item-level data with a licence was found.
provenance.identityCheck: Not possible: no independent public copy of the item-level data was found.
references: Anderson, C., Al-Gahtani, S. S., & Hubona, G. S. (2011). The value of TAM antecedents in global IS development and research. Journal of Organizational and End User Computing, 23(1), 18-37.

Al-Gahtani, S. S., Hubona, G. S., & Wang, J. (2007). Information technology (IT) in Saudi Arabia: Culture and the acceptance and use of IT. Information & Management, 44(8), 681-691. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.im.2007.09.002

Al-Gahtani, S. S., & Shih, H.-P. (2009). The influence of organizational communication openness on the post-adoption of computers. Journal of Global Information Management, 17(3), 20-41. https://doi.org/10.4018/jgim.2009070102
provenance.whatWouldUpgradeIt: Written permission from the data owners (Al-Gahtani / Hubona) or from SmartPLS GmbH, or a public deposit of the item-level data under an open licence.

proposedModel.summary: Classic TAM with attitude as a mediator. Identical to the shared Phase 0 reference model tam-v1.
proposedModel.measurementMode: reflective (SEM Lab's choice; the plain side files do not state the measurement mode)
citations: Davis, F. D. (1989). Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and user acceptance of information technology. MIS Quarterly, 13(3), 319-340. https://doi.org/10.2307/249008

Davis, F. D., Bagozzi, R. P., & Warshaw, P. R. (1989). User acceptance of computer technology: A comparison of two theoretical models. Management Science, 35(8), 982-1003. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.35.8.982
proposedModel.citationBasis: Standard literature citation; the primary articles were not opened in this session. The SmartPLS page names Davis et al. (1989) as the model source but describes the paths only in an image.
notes: USE1-USE3 are observed on 1-6 and USE4 on 1-11 while all other items are 1-7: the USE block mixes scale ranges, which matters for unstandardised results and for IPMA rescaling.

datasets.title: Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) sample data

SI.label: Social Influence (items are named SN1-SN3, i.e. subjective norm)

provenance.origin: Survey of 722 knowledge workers in Saudi Arabia (Al-Gahtani, Hubona & Wang, 2007), as stated on the SmartPLS sample-project page.
provenance.licence: None stated on the SmartPLS page. A Mendeley Data deposit by N. Richter (doi:10.17632/kcf54cgk78.1, CC BY 4.0) contains latent variable scores derived from the raw indicator data 'provided by' Al-Gahtani et al.; it does not contain the raw items and is therefore not a licence for this file.
provenance.identityCheck: Not possible: no independent public copy of the item-level data was found.
references: Al-Gahtani, S. S., Hubona, G. S., & Wang, J. (2007). Information technology (IT) in Saudi Arabia: Culture and the acceptance and use of IT. Information & Management, 44(8), 681-691. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.im.2007.09.002
provenance.whatWouldUpgradeIt: Written permission from the data owners or from SmartPLS GmbH, or a public deposit of the item-level data under an open licence.

proposedModel.summary: UTAUT main effects only: three determinants of intention, and intention plus facilitating conditions as determinants of use. The moderators of the original theory (gender, age, experience, voluntariness) are not in the data file and are therefore not specified.
proposedModel.measurementMode: reflective (SEM Lab's choice; the plain side files do not state the measurement mode)
citations: Venkatesh, V., Morris, M. G., Davis, G. B., & Davis, F. D. (2003). User acceptance of information technology: Toward a unified view. MIS Quarterly, 27(3), 425-478. https://doi.org/10.2307/30036540
proposedModel.citationBasis: Standard literature citation; the primary article was not opened in this session. The SmartPLS page lists Venkatesh et al. (2003) as the model source but shows the paths only in an image.
notes: The PLS-SEM settings file calls the SN1-SN3 block 'SI'; the GSCA settings file of the same folder calls it 'SN'. Same indicators.
USE1-USE3 are observed on 1-6 and USE4 on 1-11 while all other items are 1-7.

provenance.origin: 305 employees, organizational identification data of Bergami & Bagozzi (2000), widely reused as the GSCA demonstration data of Hwang & Takane (2004, 2014). The SmartPLS page says the data are 'taken from U.S.'; the cSEM package documentation says 'South Korean employees'. The discrepancy is unresolved because the primary article could not be opened (HTTP 403).
provenance.licence: None stated on the SmartPLS page. The same 22 variables and 305 rows are distributed on CRAN inside cSEM 0.7.1 as BergamiBagozzi2000 (package licence GPL-3) and inside gesca 1.0.5 as gesca.rick2 (package licence GPL >= 2). Neither package documents permission from the original authors.
provenance.identityCheck: Verified on 2026-11-19: the 22 non-derived columns are cell-for-cell identical, in the same row order, to cSEM 0.7.1 BergamiBagozzi2000; gesca 1.0.5 gesca.rick2 differs in exactly one cell (cei7/org_pre7). The three *_rev columns are 6 - ac_love* and exist only in the SmartPLS sample. See evidence oi-cran-comparison.json.
references: Bergami, M., & Bagozzi, R. P. (2000). Self-categorization, affective commitment and group self-esteem as distinct aspects of social identity in the organization. British Journal of Social Psychology, 39(4), 555-577. https://doi.org/10.1348/014466600164633
Hwang, H., & Takane, Y. (2004). Generalized structured component analysis. Psychometrika, 69(1), 81-99. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02295841
Hwang, H., & Takane, Y. (2014). Generalized Structured Component Analysis: A Component-Based Approach to Structural Equation Modeling. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
provenance.whatWouldUpgradeIt: Either (a) the owner accepts GPL-3 terms for this one data file and it is rebuilt from cSEM's BergamiBagozzi2000 with the GPL notice, or (b) the R engine loads cSEM::BergamiBagozzi2000 at run time so SEM Lab redistributes nothing, or (c) permission from the original authors.

proposedModel.summary: Full mediation chain used by Hwang & Takane (2004) and reproduced in the cSEM documentation example: prestige -> identification -> the two affective commitment facets.
proposedModel.measurementMode: reflective for SEM Lab's default example (cSEM's Hwang example specifies composites); the plain side files do not state the measurement mode

variants.summary: Adds direct effects of prestige on both commitment facets (the structural part of the Henseler (2021) example in the cSEM documentation, without its gender covariate and with the Hwang item assignment).
Same structure with ACL measured by ac_love1_rev, ac_love2_rev, ac_love3_rev (6 - raw) so that a higher ACL score means more commitment. Recommended for teaching the reverse-coding step.

citations: Bergami, M., & Bagozzi, R. P. (2000). Self-categorization, affective commitment and group self-esteem as distinct aspects of social identity in the organization. British Journal of Social Psychology, 39(4), 555-577. https://doi.org/10.1348/014466600164633
Hwang, H., & Takane, Y. (2004). Generalized structured component analysis. Psychometrika, 69(1), 81-99. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02295841
proposedModel.citationBasis: The three structural equations were read from the Examples section of cSEM 0.7.1 man/BergamiBagozzi2000.Rd ('Example is taken from Hwang et al. (2004)'), which was opened. The primary articles were not opened.
notes: The plain PLS-SEM settings file assigns the RAW items ac_love1-3 to 'Affective _Commitment (Love)'. In the data the raw love items correlate negatively with the joy and identification items; the *_rev columns equal 6 - raw.
With raw love items the sign of the ACL loadings and of OI -> ACL depends on the engine's sign-orientation rule. Record the rule in any reference result.
Construct names in the PLS-SEM settings file contain spaces, underscores and parentheses ('Affective _Commitment (Joy)' has a space before the underscore). Use the short codes in generated code.
gender (1 = male, 2 = female; 157/148) is a grouping variable, not an indicator.

datasets.title: American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI) 2015 sample data

provenance.origin: Sample of 8,239 consumer responses collected by the American Customer Satisfaction Index in 2015 for four industries, deposited by the ACSI researchers on Mendeley Data and described in a Data in Brief article (Morgeson, Hult, Sharma & Fornell, 2023).
provenance.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0) as stated in the Mendeley Data record. The Data in Brief article text itself is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; that licence covers the article, not the deposited data files.
provenance.identityCheck: Verified on 2026-11-19: 'ACSI Data 2015.xlsx' of Mendeley Data version 2 (sha256 53cc5ad2cf7ce8c4b1ed214e21508b7ba5059867aaedd1d9cc28ba8fc3c9bf3f) has the same 29 columns and 8,239 rows in the same order; all 185,006 value cells are identical; the 53,925 empty fields of the SmartPLS text file correspond exactly to cells that are 98, 99, '#NULL!' or empty in the deposit. See evidence acsi-mendeley-comparison.json.
provenance.attribution: Hult, Tomas; Morgeson, Forrest (2023), "The American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI): A Sample Dataset and Description", Mendeley Data, V2, doi: 10.17632/64xkbj2ry5.2. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Changes made: converted to CSV; the missing-data codes 98 and 99, SPSS '#NULL!' cells and empty cells are written as empty fields.
references: Morgeson, F. V., III, Hult, G. T. M., Sharma, U., & Fornell, C. (2023). The American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI): A sample dataset and description. Data in Brief, 48, 109123. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2023.109123
provenance.whatWouldUpgradeIt: Nothing needed. Keep the attribution text and the CC BY 4.0 link wherever the file is shown or shipped.

proposedModel.summary: ACSI base model without the complaints construct, matching the 'ACSI (modified)' / 'ACSI (without COMP)' naming of the sample files and the five constructs present in the measurement assignment.
proposedModel.measurementMode: reflective (SEM Lab's choice; the plain side files do not state the measurement mode)

variants.summary: Full base model of Fig. 1 with complaints as a single-indicator construct COMPL measured by the binary item COMP: adds CUSA -> COMPL and COMPL -> CUSL. Needs an explicit decision on how a binary single indicator is treated; not recommended as a default example.

citations: Fornell, C., Johnson, M. D., Anderson, E. W., Cha, J., & Bryant, B. E. (1996). The American Customer Satisfaction Index: Nature, purpose, and findings. Journal of Marketing, 60(4), 7-18. https://doi.org/10.1177/002224299606000403

Morgeson, F. V., III, Hult, G. T. M., Sharma, U., & Fornell, C. (2023). The American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI): A sample dataset and description. Data in Brief, 48, 109123. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2023.109123
proposedModel.citationBasis: All nine arrows of the base model were read from Fig. 1 ('The ACSI base model') of Morgeson et al. (2023), which was opened; the seven proposed paths are the seven that do not involve complaints. Fornell et al. (1996) is cited as the original model and was not opened.
notes: CUSL is measured by the single indicator REPUR: reliability and AVE are not applicable; in CB-SEM the error variance of a single indicator must be fixed.

HIGHPTOL and LOWPTOL (price tolerance) are in the data but are not assigned to CUSL in the sample. They contain the codes 26 and 101 although the data dictionary gives 0-25 as the valid range; do not use them as indicators without a documented recode.
COMP is binary (0/1) and HANDLE is answered only by complainers (1,371 of 8,239).
Missing data: the 12 model indicators have missing values, so this dataset is the natural listwise-versus-FIML fixture. The sample's own setting for missing values is MEAN_REPLACEMENT.

datasets.title: Oddjob Airways regression subset (Sarstedt & Mooi, A Concise Guide to Market Research)

provenance.origin: Subset of the Oddjob Airways case-study data (fictitious airline) that accompanies Sarstedt & Mooi (2019), A Concise Guide to Market Research, 3rd ed., Springer. SmartPLS ships it as a regression example ('1,065 observations').
provenance.licence: None found. The book's companion site offers Oddjob.sav for download under the footer 'Copyright © 2021, A Concise Guide to Market Research' with no licence or reuse statement; the SmartPLS page states none either.
provenance.identityCheck: Verified on 2026-11-19 against Oddjob.sav from the companion site (sha256 21eba3e059d5cfa17559229bb5f69294b9ec267bec2ca97159116dbd1bafcceb, 1,065 x 71): age, gender, s9, s10, s19, s21, s23 and commitment are identical in the same row order with the same missing cells; category_1/2/3 are dummy variables of 'status' (Blue/Silver/Gold). See evidence textbook-data-comparison.json.
references: Sarstedt, M., & Mooi, E. A. (2019). A concise guide to market research: The process, data, and methods using IBM SPSS Statistics (3rd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-56707-4
provenance.whatWouldUpgradeIt: A licence or written permission from the authors or Springer.
